text:
jen_support: FYI customer AcmeWidgets opened a ticket — webhook endpoint /v1/events returning 429s. They say it started ~00:02 UTC and is ongoing. Saw a single API token generate a big burst of inbound webhook deliveries.

sam_oncall: Can you paste a sample request-id and the header we should look for? Also which region?

jen_support: request id in logs: req_0a1b2c3d; region us-west-2. Customer says their webhook worker retries immediately on 5xx and they fan out to multiple endpoints, so we might be seeing concentrated TPS from 1 token.

maya_sre: Thanks. Quick hypotheses: 1) single-token fanout -> RPM/TPM hit, 2) client-side retry loop at sub-second backoff, 3) keepalive not reused and many short-lived connections -> more concurrency counted.

li_dev: Also check they aren't using per-tenant API key rotation or stamping new tokens repeatedly causing token storm. We saw similar when clients rotate tokens per message.

jen_support: Customer says they use one token but their async queue dispatcher parallelizes to 200 workers. They confirmed default retry backoff is immediate x3.

sam_oncall: Can we confirm what quota is being hit? RPM vs TPM? ratebot: Quota hit seen: token 0x... exceeded RPM 1200 and TPM 30000 windowed. Last 5m: spikes to 5k RPM.

maya_sre: That matches token-level RPM cap. Two mitigation paths: (A) advise customer to add jitter/exponential backoff + reduce parallelism, (B) temporarily increase quota for that token (if on dedicated or enterprise), (C) use our batching/queueing pattern: gateway -> single writer to webhook with controlled concurrency.

tom_acmeops: Quick question: if we apply a rate limit bump, will it mask a retry storm or just allow more failures downstream?

li_dev: Bump buys time but doesn't fix retry amplification. Recommend throttling client-side and enable server-side graceful 429 headers with Retry-After so their dispatcher can back off. We can also set per-route soft limits with 503 fallback.

jen_support: I asked for a minimal repro they can run to demonstrate. They shared a small script that does 200 parallel POSTs to our webhook endpoint using the same token with no backoff.

sam_oncall: Can someone run a controlled replay in staging to confirm behavior? If we can reproduce, we can confirm whether connection reuse is inflating TPM counts (HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 differences).

maya_sre: I'll spin a staging replay. Quick checks I'll run: `curl -v` capture `x-request-id`, `x-rate-limit-*` headers, and server logs for token bucket drops. Also check edge batchers for inflight slot occupancy.

li_dev: When you replay, include a variation with HTTP/2 multiplexing and one with short-lived TCP connections to see effect on concurrent stream counting.

jen_support: Customer asked if we can provide recommended client config. Drafted this: "reduce parallel workers to <= 20 for async webhook delivery; implement exponential backoff with base 200ms and jitter; respect Retry-After; use connection pooling/HTTP/2; optionally add a small queue with rate-limiter token bucket on their side."

tom_acmeops: We'll try that today and share results. If the issue persists we'll ask for a temporary quota bump while we migrate to new worker config.

maya_sre: Replay results: reproduced 429s with the 200-parallel immediate retries. TPM accounting shows large jump when connections are short-lived; HTTP/2 multiplexing collapsed the same traffic into fewer slots and reduced TPM pressure.

sam_oncall: Good. Action items: 1) jen_support send the recommended client config + this thread summary to customer, 2) maja_sre (typo: maya) open internal runbook note about webhook retry amplification, 3) if customer requests, offer a temporary token-level quota increase for 24h while they roll config.

jen_support: Sending summary now. Also flagged support ticket for quota bump approval if they ask. :white_check_mark:

tom_acmeops: Confirmed — we'll implement backoff + reduce concurrency and test. Thanks everyone.

li_dev: Follow-up note: include sample code snippet for exponential backoff:
```
const backoff = (attempt) => Math.min(200 * 2 ** attempt + Math.floor(Math.random()*100), 5000)
// on 429 -> wait backoff(attempt) ms then retry
```

maya_sre: Closing loop: metrics we expect to see after mitigation: sustained RPM < 1200, retry storms eliminated, fewer 429 spikes, and better tail latency. Reopen here if we still see edge-ratecap triggers.

sam_oncall: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
